title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 9 Some Applications of Trigonometry (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
short_title: Class 10 Maths · Ch 9 Some Applications of Trigonometry
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number. No calculator.

S1.name: Elevation, depression, which ratio
S1.tip: Elevation: look up; depression: look down; both from the horizontal. Depression from the top = elevation from the bottom (alternate angles). Height + distance → tan; string/ladder → sin or cos.

S2.name: One triangle: height and distance
S2.tip: tan θ = height/distance: 15 m away at 60° → 15√3 m. Keep the answer in √3 form unless a value is given.

S3.name: Shadows and the Sun's angle
S3.tip: Shadow = height → 45°; shadow = √3 × height → 30°; height = √3 × shadow → 60°. Same time → same height/shadow ratio.

S4.name: Strings, ladders and kites
S4.tip: The string, rope or ladder is the hypotenuse: sin θ = height/length, cos θ = ground/length. tan θ = 12/5 → sin θ = 12/13.
S4.ncert: NCERT Example 2; Exercise 9.1 Q1, Q3, Q5

S5.name: The observer's height
S5.tip: Work from the eyes: use (height − eye height), then add the eye height back at the end.

S6.name: Two angles, same side
S6.tip: Same side: distances at 30° and 60° are h√3 and h/√3; they differ by 2h/√3. Speed = distance moved / time.
S6.ncert: NCERT Example 5; Exercise 9.1 Q11, Q13, Q14

S7.name: Opposite sides
S7.tip: Opposite sides: add the two horizontal distances (bridge over a river, ships on both sides, poles across a road).

S8.name: Two heights: tower on a building, depression of top and bottom
S8.tip: Two heights share one base. Tower on a building: 45° to the bottom gives the base; 60° to the top gives the total. Depression of top and bottom: PD√3 = PD + (short height).

S9.name: Time, speed and case studies
S9.tip: 30° then 60° after t at uniform speed → t/2 more to the foot. Case studies: subtract the eye height first; angles are only 30°, 45°, 60°.

questions.question: The angle of elevation of an object is the angle between:
questions.explanation: Elevation and depression are both measured from the horizontal.
options: the line of sight and the vertical
the line of sight and the horizontal

questions.question: Looking down from a balcony at a car on the road, the angle your line of sight makes with the horizontal is the:
questions.explanation: Below the horizontal → angle of depression.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; the horizontals at the top and at sea level are parallel, so the angles are alternate.
questions.assertion: The angle of depression of a boat from the top of a cliff equals the angle of elevation of the cliff top from the boat.
questions.reason: They are alternate angles between parallel horizontal lines.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: A kite's height h and the angle θ of its string with the ground are known. The string length L is found from:
questions.explanation: The string is the hypotenuse; height is opposite θ → sin θ = h/L.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: string or ladder → sin or cos.

questions.question: From a point 20 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top is 45°. Find the height of the tower in metres.
From a point 12 m from a pole, the angle of elevation of its top is 60°. The height of the pole is:
The angle of elevation of the top of a 50 m tower from a point on the ground is 30°. The distance of the point from the foot is:
A tower is 10√3 m high. From a point on the ground its top is seen at 60°. Find the distance of the point from the foot of the tower in metres.
If the shadow of a pole is equal to its height, the Sun's angle of elevation is:
questions.explanation: tan θ = 1 → 45° (a 2024 board type).

questions.question: A 9 m pole casts a shadow 3√3 m long. The Sun's angle of elevation is:
questions.explanation: tan θ = 9/(3√3) = √3 → 60° (a 2023 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: A 6 m pole casts a 4 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 30 m shadow. Find the height of the tower in metres.
questions.explanation: Same Sun angle → height/shadow is the same: 6/4 = h/30 → h = 45 (a 2024 board type).
questions.remediation: Video part 2: same time, same angle.

questions.question: The ratio of the height of a pole to its shadow is 1 : √3. The Sun's angle of elevation is:
questions.explanation: tan θ = 1/√3 → 30° (a 2024 board type).

questions.question: A kite is flying at a height of 40 m. Its string makes an angle of 30° with the ground. Find the length of the string in metres.
A 20 m rope is tied from the top of a vertical pole to the ground and makes 30° with the ground. The height of the pole is:
questions.explanation: sin 30° = h/20 → h = 10 (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q1).

questions.question: A 10 m ladder leans against a wall making 60° with the ground. The height it reaches on the wall is:
A kite string 26 m long makes an angle θ with the ground, where tan θ = 12/5. Find the height of the kite in metres.
questions.explanation: tan θ = 12/5 → sin θ = 12/13 → h = 26 × 12/13 = 24 (SQP 2026-27 Q17 type, new numbers).

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: √(36 + 64) = 10; the right angle at the wall is why Pythagoras applies (a 2025 board type).
questions.assertion: A ladder whose foot is 6 m from a wall and which reaches 8 m up the wall is 10 m long.
questions.reason: The ladder, the wall and the ground form a right triangle.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: An observer whose eyes are 2 m above the ground stands 28 m from a building. The angle of elevation of the top of the building from her eyes is 45°. Find the height of the building in metres.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: add the eye height back.

questions.question: A 1.5 m tall girl stands 30√3 m from a tower. The angle of elevation of its top from her eyes is 30°. The height of the tower is:
A 1.6 m tall man walks towards a 31.6 m tall tower. The angle of elevation of its top from his eyes changes from 30° to 60°. The distance he walked is k√3 m. Find k.
questions.explanation: Above eye level: 30 m. Distances 30√3 and 30/√3 = 10√3 → walked 20√3 (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q6 type).

questions.question: The shadow of a tower is 20 m longer when the Sun's altitude is 30° than when it is 60°. The height of the tower is:
questions.explanation: h√3 − h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 20 → h = 10√3 (NCERT Example 5 type).

questions.question: From the top of a 60 m tower, the angles of depression of two cars on the same side are 30° and 60°. The distance between the cars is k√3 m. Find k.
questions.explanation: Distances 60√3 and 60/√3 = 20√3 → 40√3 (a 2023 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: A TV tower stands on one bank of a canal. From the opposite bank its top is at 60°; from a point 20 m further back on the same line it is at 30°. Find the width of the canal in metres.
questions.explanation: h = x√3 = (x + 20)/√3 → 3x = x + 20 → x = 10 (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q11).

questions.question: A plane flies horizontally at a height of 1500√3 m. Its angle of elevation from a point on the ground changes from 60° to 30° in 15 seconds. Find its speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: Distances 1500 and 4500 → 3000 m in 15 s = 200 m/s (a 2024 board type).

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a tower's top is 30° from a point; after walking 40 m towards the tower it is 60°. The height of the tower is:
From a point on a bridge 5 m above the water, the angles of depression of the two banks on opposite sides are both 45°. The width of the river is:
questions.explanation: Each part = 5 → 10.

questions.question: From a point on a bridge 6 m above the banks, the angles of depression of the banks on opposite sides are 30° and 60°. The width of the river is k√3 m. Find k.
questions.explanation: 6√3 + 6/√3 = 6√3 + 2√3 = 8√3 (a 2024 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: Two poles of equal height stand on either side of a 40 m wide road. From a point on the road between them, the angles of elevation of their tops are 60° and 30°. The height of each pole is k√3 m. Find k.
questions.explanation: x√3 = (40 − x)/√3 → x = 10 → h = 10√3 (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q10 type).

questions.question: From the top of a 30 m lighthouse, the angles of depression of two ships on opposite sides are 30° and 60°. The distance between the ships is:
From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of a flagstaff on a 10 m building are 45° and 60°. The height of the top of the flagstaff above the ground is k√3 m. Find k.
From a point P, the top of a 12 m building is at 30°, and the top of a flagstaff on it is at 45°. The length of the flagstaff is:
questions.explanation: AP = 12√3; 45° → total 12√3 → flagstaff 12√3 − 12 (NCERT Example 4 type).

questions.question: From the top of a 12 m building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. The height of the tower is:
questions.explanation: 45° → distance 12; above the roof 12√3 → 12 + 12√3 (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q12 type).

questions.question: From the top of a tower, the angles of depression of the top and the bottom of a 10 m building are 30° and 60°. Find the height of the tower in metres.
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: d = 60/√3 = 20√3 → building = 20√3 × 1/√3 = 20; the shared base is the key step (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q9 type).
questions.assertion: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of a 60 m tower is 30°, and of the top of the tower from the foot of the building is 60°. Then the building is 20 m high.
questions.reason: Both right triangles share the same horizontal distance between the feet.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: A 2 m statue stands on a pedestal. From a point on the ground, the top of the statue is at 60° and the top of the pedestal at 45°. The height of the pedestal is a(√3 + 1) m. Find a.
questions.explanation: h√3 = h + 2 → h = 2/(√3 − 1) = √3 + 1 → a = 1 (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q8 type).

questions.question: A car moves at a uniform speed towards a tower. From the top, its angle of depression is 30°, and 10 seconds later it is 60°. How many more seconds will it take to reach the foot of the tower?
questions.explanation: Covered 2h/√3 in 10 s; remaining h/√3 → 5 s (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q15 type).

questions.question: A man on a cliff sees a boat approaching at an angle of depression of 30°; 4 minutes later it is 60°. At the same speed, the boat reaches the foot of the cliff in:
questions.explanation: Remaining distance is half of what was covered → 2 minutes (a 2024 board type).

questions.question: Case study: a 37 m monument; a visitor whose eyes are 1 m above the ground stands 36 m from its base. Find the angle of elevation of the top from the visitor's eyes, in degrees.
questions.explanation: tan θ = (37 − 1)/36 = 1 → 45° (SQP 2025-26 Q38 type, new numbers).
questions.remediation: Video part 9: subtract the eye height first.

questions.question: Same monument (37 m, eyes 1 m up). If the angle of elevation is 60°, the visitor stands from the base at:
A balloon moves horizontally at a constant height, 30√3 m above a girl's eyes. Its angle of elevation falls from 60° to 30° in 10 seconds. Find the balloon's speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: Distances 30 and 90 → 60 m in 10 s = 6 m/s (NCERT Exercise 9.1 Q14 / SQP 2024-25 Q34 type).
questions.remediation: Video part 5: two angles, same side.
